questions.title: Is f(x) a Legitimate Density - the two properties of a probability density function
Probability Is Area - P(c < x < d) as base times height under a flat density
P(x = c) Is Zero - a single point has no width, so no area
The Complement Rule - P(X > x) = 1 - P(X < x)
The Cumulative Distribution Function - P(X <= x) = (x - a) / (b - a)
Uniform Mean and Standard Deviation - mu = (a+b)/2 and sigma = sqrt((b-a)^2/12)
Uniform Quartiles and Median - the percentiles of X ~ U(a, b)
The Two Sanity Checks - catch a probability bigger than 1 or negative
Height Is a Density, Not a Probability - multiply by the width
Pre-FRQ Grade a Uniform Reasoning - a flat-density scenario with a grading checklist, where the student grades four sample responses against the rubric instead of writing one
